chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Hammad ibn Zayd, from 'Abd Allah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, who said:

Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام led us in prayer in the mosque of Banu Kahil. He recited Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim aloud twice, performed qunut in the fajr prayer, and gave one taslim toward the direction of the qiblah.

key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: The fajr prayer, the dawn salat (prayer).
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةَ: The direction of prayer toward which one faces.
key_terms.بِبِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ: The basmalah, recited here aloud in the prayer.
key_terms.فَجَهَرَ: He recited aloud, indicating audible pronunciation in prayer.
key_terms.وَسَلَّمَ وَاحِدَةً: He gave one taslim, meaning a single salutation to conclude the prayer.
key_terms.وَقَنَتَ: He performed qunut, the supplicatory standing in prayer.

ai.seo_question: How did Abu 'Abd Allah Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام perform fajr prayer according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the prayer practice of Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام in congregation. It indicates audible recitation of Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim, the performance of qunut in fajr, and a single taslim toward the qiblah, all of which are significant in discussions of Shia prayer rulings.
